Read me.Detail: Glossary of the core elements of a P&ID: equipment symbols, instrumentation and control, valves, and line conventions.
Pick the symbol or tag from the relevant sheet. Each row names the standard it follows in the last column.
Compiled from general knowledge of the standards listed below, not copied from them. Verify against your company's licensed copies before issuing as a project legend sheet.

ISA-5.1 covers instrumentation only. No ISA or current ASME standard fixes one set of equipment outlines; industry practice follows PIP PIC001 or ISO 10628-2. Outlines here are the commonly used ones.
ANSI/ISA-5.1 - Instrumentation Symbols and Identification: instrument bubbles, tag letters, signal lines, valve and actuator symbols.
ISA-5.2 / ISA-5.3 / ISA-5.4 - binary logic diagrams, shared display and computer symbols, instrument loop diagrams.
ASME B31.3 - Process Piping: basis for pipe specifications referenced in line numbers.
ASME B36.10M / B36.19M - pipe sizes (NPS) and schedules for carbon and stainless steel pipe.
ASME B16.5 - flange pressure classes (150, 300, 600 ...) used in pipe specs. ASME B16.34 - valve ratings.
ASME BPVC Section VIII - pressure vessel design and overpressure protection (basis for PSVs shown on the P&ID).
PIP PIC001 - P&ID Documentation Criteria: widely used format, equipment symbols and tagging practice.
ISO 10628-2 - graphical symbols for process plant diagrams. ISO 14617 - graphical symbols for diagrams.
ASME Y32.11 - graphical symbols for process flow diagrams (older standard, withdrawn; some legacy legends still cite it).

The request describes dashed or dotted lines for pneumatic, electric or signal links. ISA-5.1 distinguishes them: electrical is dashed, pneumatic is solid with double slash marks, data links carry small circles.

ISA-5.1 letters.Meaning: Unclassified (define on legend; here XV = on/off shutdown valve)
